tasks.title: Initialize TypeScript Project & Install Dependencies
tasks.description: Set up the Node.js/TypeScript project with all required dependencies, configure tsconfig.json for strict mode with ES2022 target, set up the module structure from LLD Section 4, create package.json with bin entry for `secsee` CLI, and configure build scripts.
tasks.details: Create the project at the root. Use `npm init -y`, then install all production and dev dependencies. Configure tsconfig.json and create the full src/ directory structure per LLD Section 4.
tasks.testStrategy: Run `npm run build` — must compile with zero errors. Run `npx secsee --help` — must show CLI help. Verify all directories exist.

subtasks.title: Run npm init and configure package.json
subtasks.description: Run `npm init -y` in project root. Update package.json: set name to 'secsee', version '0.1.0', description 'AI-powered E2E integration tester via MCP', main 'dist/index.js', types 'dist/index.d.ts'. Add bin entry: { "secsee": "./dist/cli.js" }. Add scripts: "build": "tsc", "dev": "tsx watch src/index.ts", "start": "node dist/index.js", "cli": "tsx src/cli.ts". Set type to 'module'. Set engines: { "node": ">=20.0.0" }. Add files: ["dist/"].

subtasks.title: Install production dependencies
subtasks.description: npm install @modelcontextprotocol/sdk zod commander dockerode playwright ts-morph @babel/parser pg mysql2 mongodb js-yaml. These are the core runtime dependencies: MCP SDK for server protocol, zod for schema validation, commander for CLI, dockerode for Docker API, playwright for browser automation, ts-morph for TypeScript AST parsing, @babel/parser for JavaScript AST, pg/mysql2/mongodb for DB verification, js-yaml for docker-compose parsing.

subtasks.title: Install dev dependencies
subtasks.description: npm install -D typescript @types/node @types/pg @types/js-yaml tsx vitest. TypeScript compiler, Node.js types, tsx for development (watch mode without build), vitest for unit testing.

subtasks.title: Configure tsconfig.json
subtasks.description: Create tsconfig.json with: { "compilerOptions": { "target": "ES2022", "module": "NodeNext", "moduleResolution": "NodeNext", "strict": true, "outDir": "dist", "rootDir": "src", "declaration": true, "declarationMap": true, "sourceMap": true, "esModuleInterop": true, "skipLibCheck": true, "forceConsistentCasingInFileNames": true, "resolveJsonModule": true }, "include": ["src/**/*"], "exclude": ["node_modules", "dist"] }.

subtasks.title: Create full src/ directory structure per LLD Section 4
subtasks.description: Create all directories: src/, src/server/, src/server/tools/, src/analyzer/, src/analyzer/strategies/, src/analyzer/visitors/, src/docker/, src/tester/, src/tester/api/, src/tester/api/validators/, src/tester/frontend/, src/db/, src/report/, src/config/, src/types/, src/utils/. Create placeholder index.ts files in each directory with empty exports.

subtasks.title: Create entry point files (src/index.ts, src/cli.ts)
subtasks.description: Create src/index.ts with minimal MCP server bootstrap (just a console.error('SecSee starting...')). Create src/cli.ts with shebang #!/usr/bin/env node and minimal commander setup that shows --help. Verify `npm run build` compiles both. Verify `node dist/cli.js --help` shows output.

subtasks.title: Create .gitignore and .npmignore
subtasks.description: Create .gitignore with: node_modules/, dist/, .secsee/test-report.*, .secsee/screenshots/, .secsee/working.md, .secsee/working.json, .env, *.tgz. Create .npmignore with: src/, .taskmaster/, docs/, .secsee/, tests/, *.test.ts.

subtasks.title: Verify build and CLI smoke test
subtasks.description: Run `npm run build` — must compile with zero TypeScript errors. Run `node dist/cli.js --help` — must display secsee command help. Run `npm pack` — must create a valid tarball. Verify all files in dist/ match src/ structure.

tasks.title: Define All Shared TypeScript Interfaces & Types
tasks.description: Create src/types/index.ts with all shared interfaces from LLD Section 3.
tasks.details: Implement every interface from LLD Sections 3.1, 3.2, 3.3.
tasks.testStrategy: TypeScript compiles with zero errors. Import all types in a test file and instantiate mock objects.

subtasks.title: Define EndpointDefinition and related types (LLD 3.1)
subtasks.description: In src/types/index.ts: Define HttpMethod type ('GET'|'POST'|'PUT'|'PATCH'|'DELETE'). Define SchemaField interface with type ('string'|'number'|'boolean'|'object'|'array'), required (boolean), example (any), children (Record<string, SchemaField>). Define AuthScheme type with kind ('jwt'|'api-key'|'session'|'oauth2'|'basic'), headerName (string), tokenPrefix (string). Define DbInteraction with table (string), operation ('create'|'read'|'update'|'delete'), fields (string[]), service (string). Define OutboundCall with targetUrl (string), method (HttpMethod), service (string), triggeredBy (string). Define EndpointDefinition per LLD 3.1 with all nested request/response schemas.

subtasks.title: Define Test Result types (LLD 3.2)
subtasks.description: Define ApiTestResult with endpoint, method, status ('pass'|'fail'|'skip'|'error'), request object, expectedResponse, actualResponse (including latencyMs), dbValidation (passed boolean, diff), webhookValidation, validationErrors string[]. Define PageTestResult with url, normalizedUrl, depth, screenshot path, interactiveElements (ElementInfo[]), formsFound (FormInfo[]), formTestResults (FormTestResult[]), networkRequests (NetworkEntry[]), networkValidation (NetworkValidationResult[]), consoleErrors (string[]), loadTimeMs. Define NetworkEntry with url, method, headers, postData, responseStatus, responseHeaders, responseBody, timestamp, type. Define FormInfo with action, method, fields array of {name, type, required, placeholder}. Define ElementInfo with tag, selector, text, href, type. Define FormTestResult with formInfo, dataSubmitted, networkRequest, networkResponse, validationErrors, passed.

subtasks.title: Define Configuration types (LLD 3.3)
subtasks.description: Define SecseeConfig per LLD 3.3 with dockerComposePath, frontendUrl, services (ServiceConfig[]), testCredentials, excludePaths, crawl config (maxDepth, maxPages, waitForNetworkIdle, screenshotOnEveryPage), timeout, browser ('chromium'|'firefox'|'webkit'), parallel, db (DbConnectionConfig[]). Define ServiceConfig with name, path, framework, type ('backend'|'frontend'|'database'), port, baseUrl. Define DbConnectionConfig with type ('postgres'|'mysql'|'mongodb'), connectionString, name.

subtasks.title: Define Crawler, Docker, Validation, and Report types
subtasks.description: Define CrawlState with queue (CrawlTarget[]), visited (Set<string>), results (PageTestResult[]), networkLog (NetworkEntry[]). Define CrawlTarget with url, normalizedUrl, depth, referrer, elementSelector. Define ContainerState per LLD 2.4 with name, status enum, port, healthCheckAttempts, error. Define ValidationContext with endpoint, request, response, dbBefore (DbSnapshot), dbAfter (DbSnapshot). Define ValidationResult with validatorName, passed, message, details. Define DbSnapshot with table, rows (Record<string,any>[]), timestamp. Define DbDiff with inserted, deleted, modified arrays. Define TestReport with summary, apiResults, frontendResults, networkValidation, issues, generatedAt. Define Issue with severity ('critical'|'high'|'medium'|'low'), message, endpoint, page, details. Define Screenshot with path, url, timestamp. Define NetworkValidationResult with networkEntry, contract (EndpointDefinition), passed, mismatches (string[]).

subtasks.title: Define ProjectAnalysis aggregate type
subtasks.description: Define ProjectAnalysis as the top-level output of the analyzer: { projectRoot: string, services: ServiceAnalysis[], discoveredAt: number }. Define ServiceAnalysis with name, path, framework, type, endpoints (EndpointDefinition[]), dbInteractions (DbInteraction[]), outboundCalls (OutboundCall[]), authScheme (AuthScheme | null). This is the type that feeds into working.md generation and test generation.

tasks.title: Implement Configuration System with Zod Validation
tasks.description: Build src/config/schema.ts with Zod schemas and src/config/loader.ts for config file management.
tasks.details: Zod schemas mirroring SecseeConfig. Loader reads .secsee/config.json, validates, provides defaults.
tasks.testStrategy: Unit test: loadConfig with valid/invalid/missing JSON.

subtasks.title: Define Zod schemas in src/config/schema.ts
subtasks.description: Import z from 'zod'. Define DbConnectionConfigSchema: z.object({ type: z.enum(['postgres','mysql','mongodb']), connectionString: z.string(), name: z.string() }). Define ServiceConfigSchema: z.object({ name: z.string(), path: z.string(), framework: z.string().optional(), type: z.enum(['backend','frontend','database']), port: z.number().optional(), baseUrl: z.string().optional() }). Define CrawlConfigSchema: z.object({ maxDepth: z.number().default(10), maxPages: z.number().default(100), waitForNetworkIdle: z.boolean().default(true), screenshotOnEveryPage: z.boolean().default(true) }). Define SecseeConfigSchema: z.object({ dockerComposePath: z.string().default('docker-compose.yml'), frontendUrl: z.string().url(), services: z.array(ServiceConfigSchema).default([]), testCredentials: z.object({ username: z.string(), password: z.string() }).optional(), excludePaths: z.array(z.string()).default([]), crawl: CrawlConfigSchema.default({}), timeout: z.number().default(30000), browser: z.enum(['chromium','firefox','webkit']).default('chromium'), parallel: z.number().default(1), db: z.array(DbConnectionConfigSchema).default([]) }). Export all schemas and inferred types.

subtasks.title: Implement config loader in src/config/loader.ts
subtasks.description: Import fs/promises, path, and SecseeConfigSchema. Function `async loadConfig(projectRoot: string): Promise<SecseeConfig>`: construct configPath as path.join(projectRoot, '.secsee', 'config.json'). Try to read file with fs.readFile. If file not found (ENOENT), return SecseeConfigSchema.parse({ frontendUrl: 'http://localhost:3000' }) as default. If file exists, JSON.parse the content, run through SecseeConfigSchema.parse() which applies defaults and validates. Catch ZodError and rethrow with human-readable message including field paths. Export loadConfig.

subtasks.title: Implement initConfig for project initialization
subtasks.description: Function `async initConfig(projectRoot: string): Promise<void>`: Create .secsee/ directory if not exists. Write default config.json with commented descriptions (as a clean JSON with all fields showing defaults). Check if .gitignore exists — if yes, append '.secsee/test-report.*', '.secsee/screenshots/', '.secsee/working.md' if not already present. If .gitignore doesn't exist, create it with those entries. Print 'Initialized .secsee/config.json — edit to configure your project.'

subtasks.title: Write unit tests for config system
subtasks.description: Using vitest: Test loadConfig with valid config file returns typed object with correct values. Test loadConfig with partial config applies defaults (e.g., missing crawl config gets defaults). Test loadConfig with invalid field throws ZodError. Test loadConfig with missing file returns defaults. Test initConfig creates directory and file. Test initConfig appends to existing .gitignore without duplicating entries.

tasks.title: Build MCP Server Core with StdioServerTransport
tasks.description: Implement the MCP server entry point using McpServer from @modelcontextprotocol/sdk with StdioServerTransport.
tasks.details: Use McpServer class, register tools with Zod input schemas, connect via StdioServerTransport.
tasks.testStrategy: Server starts on stdio. MCP inspector returns all 9 tools.

subtasks.title: Implement createServer() in src/server/mcp-server.ts
subtasks.description: Import { McpServer } from '@modelcontextprotocol/sdk/server' and { z } from 'zod'. Create exported function createServer() that instantiates: const server = new McpServer({ name: 'secsee', version: '0.1.0' }, { capabilities: { logging: {} } }). Return server. This function will be called by both the stdio entry point and tests.

subtasks.title: Register all 9 placeholder MCP tools
subtasks.description: In createServer(), register tools using server.registerTool(name, { description, inputSchema }, handler). Tools to register: (1) analyze_project — inputSchema: z.object({ projectRoot: z.string().describe('Absolute path to project root') }). (2) spin_up_services — same input. (3) tear_down_services — input + removeVolumes: z.boolean().optional(). (4) test_apis — same input. (5) test_frontend — input + headed: z.boolean().optional(). (6) test_single_endpoint — input + path: z.string(), method: z.string(). (7) test_page — input + url: z.string(). (8) generate_report — input + format: z.enum(['markdown','json','both']).optional(). (9) update_working_doc — same input. Each handler returns { content: [{ type: 'text', text: 'Not implemented yet' }] } as placeholder.

subtasks.title: Implement stdio entry point in src/index.ts
subtasks.description: Import { StdioServerTransport } from '@modelcontextprotocol/sdk/server'. Import createServer from './server/mcp-server.js'. Main function: create server via createServer(), create transport via new StdioServerTransport(), await server.connect(transport), console.error('SecSee MCP Server running on stdio'). Wrap in try/catch — on error, console.error and process.exit(1). Register process.on('SIGINT') and process.on('SIGTERM') for graceful shutdown (call server.close() if available, then process.exit(0)). IMPORTANT: All logging via console.error — stdout is reserved for JSON-RPC protocol messages.

subtasks.title: Test MCP server starts and lists tools
subtasks.description: Verify: `npm run build` succeeds. Running `node dist/index.js` starts without crashing (exits cleanly on SIGINT). If MCP inspector available, connect and verify list_tools returns all 9 tools with correct names and schemas. Otherwise, write a simple test that imports createServer, creates it, and verifies tool count.

tasks.title: Build CLI Entry Point with Commander.js
tasks.description: Implement src/cli.ts with commander.js providing subcommands mirroring MCP tools.
tasks.details: Commander subcommands: init, analyze, up, down, test, test:api, test:ui, report.
tasks.testStrategy: secsee --help shows all commands. secsee init creates config.

subtasks.title: Set up commander program with global options
subtasks.description: In src/cli.ts: Add shebang #!/usr/bin/env node. Import { Command } from 'commander'. Create: const program = new Command('secsee').version('0.1.0').description('AI-powered E2E integration tester'). Add global option: .option('-p, --project <path>', 'Project root directory', process.cwd()). Add global option: .option('-v, --verbose', 'Enable verbose logging', false).

subtasks.title: Implement init command
subtasks.description: program.command('init').description('Initialize SecSee configuration in current project').action(async () => { const projectRoot = program.opts().project; await initConfig(projectRoot); console.log('SecSee initialized. Edit .secsee/config.json to configure.'); }). Import initConfig from '../config/loader.js'.

subtasks.title: Implement analyze, up, down, test, test:api, test:ui, report commands
subtasks.description: Add all remaining commands as stubs that load config and print 'Not implemented yet — coming in Phase N': analyze (Phase 2), up/down (Phase 3), test:api (Phase 4), test:ui (Phase 5), test (Phase 4+5), report (Phase 6). Each command should: load config via loadConfig(program.opts().project), log the config loaded message, then print the stub. Add command aliases where useful: 'up' for spin-up, 'down' for tear-down.

subtasks.title: Wire program.parse() and verify CLI works
subtasks.description: At bottom of cli.ts: program.parse(process.argv). Build and test: `node dist/cli.js --help` shows all commands. `node dist/cli.js init` creates .secsee/config.json. `node dist/cli.js analyze` prints stub message. Verify shebang works: `chmod +x dist/cli.js && ./dist/cli.js --help`.

tasks.title: Implement IFrameworkAnalyzer Interface & AnalyzerRegistry
tasks.description: Create the analyzer interface and plugin registry from LLD Section 2.1 and 2.3.
tasks.details: Strategy pattern interface with detect/extract methods. Registry with priority-based resolution.
tasks.testStrategy: Register mock analyzers. resolve() returns highest priority. Throws on no match.

subtasks.title: Define IFrameworkAnalyzer interface in src/analyzer/interface.ts
subtasks.description: Export interface IFrameworkAnalyzer with: name: string (e.g., 'express', 'fastapi'); detect(servicePath: string): Promise<boolean>; extractEndpoints(servicePath: string): Promise<EndpointDefinition[]>; extractDbInteractions(servicePath: string): Promise<DbInteraction[]>; extractOutboundCalls(servicePath: string): Promise<OutboundCall[]>; extractAuthScheme(servicePath: string): Promise<AuthScheme | null>. Import types from '../types/index.js'.

subtasks.title: Implement AnalyzerRegistry class in src/analyzer/registry.ts
subtasks.description: Class AnalyzerRegistry: private analyzers: Array<{ analyzer: IFrameworkAnalyzer, priority: number }> = []. Method register(analyzer, priority): push and sort by priority descending. Method async resolve(servicePath): iterate analyzers, call analyzer.detect(servicePath), return first that returns true. If none match, throw new AnalyzerNotFoundError(servicePath). Method async resolveAll(servicePath): return all matching analyzers. Method getRegistered(): return analyzer names and priorities for debugging.

subtasks.title: Create AnalyzerNotFoundError in src/utils/errors.ts
subtasks.description: Export class AnalyzerNotFoundError extends Error: constructor takes servicePath, sets message to `No analyzer found for service at: ${servicePath}`. Add property servicePath for programmatic access.

subtasks.title: Create default registry singleton
subtasks.description: At bottom of registry.ts or in a separate src/analyzer/default-registry.ts: export const defaultRegistry = new AnalyzerRegistry(). Register built-in analyzers with priorities: ExpressAnalyzer (100), FastAPIAnalyzer (90), FlaskAnalyzer (80), GenericAnalyzer (0 — lowest, always matches). Import will be lazy — initially register only the analyzers that have been implemented.

tasks.title: Implement Service Discovery & Project Scanner
tasks.description: Build project scanning logic per LLD Section 5.1.
tasks.details: Walk directories, detect services by markers, delegate to AnalyzerRegistry.
tasks.testStrategy: Mock project with Express service and React frontend detected correctly.

subtasks.title: Implement directory walker with framework detection
subtasks.description: In src/analyzer/scanner.ts: Function async scanProject(projectRoot, registry): Walk projectRoot recursively (max depth 3). Skip directories: node_modules, .git, dist, build, __pycache__, .venv, .next, .secsee, .taskmaster. For each directory, check for framework markers: (1) Read package.json if exists → check dependencies for 'express', '@nestjs/core', 'fastify', 'koa', 'hapi' (Node backends), 'react', 'vue', 'next', 'angular', '@sveltejs/kit' (frontends). (2) Read requirements.txt if exists → check for 'fastapi', 'flask', 'django'. (3) Read pyproject.toml if exists → same checks in [tool.poetry.dependencies]. (4) Check for Dockerfile → marks as deployable service. Return discovered ServiceInfo[] with name (dirname), path, detectedFramework, type guess.

subtasks.title: Implement docker-compose.yml service matching
subtasks.description: If docker-compose.yml exists at projectRoot, parse it (js-yaml) and extract service names. Match compose service names to discovered directories by: exact name match, build context path match, or image name containing directory name. Enrich ServiceInfo with compose metadata: image, ports (host:container), environment variables, depends_on, healthcheck config. This helps map running containers back to service directories.

subtasks.title: Integrate scanner with AnalyzerRegistry
subtasks.description: For each discovered service, call registry.resolve(servicePath). If resolved, attach the analyzer to ServiceInfo. If no analyzer found (AnalyzerNotFoundError), log warning and continue — don't fail the entire scan. Return ServiceInfo[] with optional analyzer attached. Function async analyzeProject(projectRoot, registry): calls scanProject, then for each service with an analyzer, runs all extract methods (endpoints, dbInteractions, outboundCalls, authScheme). Assembles and returns ProjectAnalysis.

subtasks.title: Write unit tests for scanner
subtasks.description: Create a temp directory with: (1) an 'api' folder containing package.json with express dep → detected as Express backend. (2) a 'web' folder with package.json with react dep → detected as frontend. (3) a node_modules folder → must be skipped. (4) docker-compose.yml referencing 'api' and 'web' services. Verify scanProject returns 2 services with correct types. Verify compose matching enriches with ports.

tasks.title: Implement ExpressAnalyzer with ts-morph AST Parsing
tasks.description: Build Express.js analyzer using ts-morph for AST traversal per LLD 2.1 and 2.2.
tasks.details: Use ts-morph SyntaxKind.CallExpression to find app.get(), router.post(), etc.
tasks.testStrategy: Parse sample Express app. All endpoints, DB calls, outbound calls extracted correctly.

subtasks.title: Implement detect() for Express
subtasks.description: In src/analyzer/strategies/express.ts: Class ExpressAnalyzer implements IFrameworkAnalyzer. name = 'express'. Method detect(servicePath): Read package.json at servicePath. Check if 'express' exists in dependencies or devDependencies. Also check for '@types/express' in devDependencies as secondary signal. Return boolean.

subtasks.title: Implement route extraction using ts-morph
subtasks.description: Method extractEndpoints(servicePath): Create ts-morph Project, add all .ts and .js files from servicePath (excluding node_modules, dist, test). For each SourceFile, call sourceFile.getDescendantsOfKind(SyntaxKind.CallExpression). Filter for calls where expression text matches patterns: 'app.get', 'app.post', 'app.put', 'app.delete', 'app.patch', 'router.get', 'router.post', 'router.put', 'router.delete', 'router.patch', 'app.use'. For each matched call: Extract method from the property name (get/post/put/delete/patch). Extract path from first argument — if StringLiteral, use getText(). If TemplateLiteral, extract template parts. Extract middleware names from middle arguments. Extract handler function (last argument). Build EndpointDefinition with method, path, source file info.

subtasks.title: Implement request/response schema inference from handler body
subtasks.description: For each extracted handler function, analyze its body using ts-morph: Find req.body access → PropertyAccessExpression where expression is 'req' and name is 'body'. If destructured (const { name, email } = req.body), extract field names. Find req.params, req.query, req.headers access similarly. For response: find res.json(), res.send() calls and inspect argument shape. Find res.status() calls to infer status codes. Build request/response schemas as SchemaField records. Types are inferred as 'string' by default unless TypeScript type annotations are available.

subtasks.title: Implement DB interaction detection
subtasks.description: Method extractDbInteractions(servicePath): Scan all files for ORM call patterns. Prisma: find calls like prisma.user.create(), prisma.post.findMany() — extract model name and operation. Sequelize: User.findAll(), User.create() patterns. Mongoose: User.find(), new User().save(). Knex: knex('users').select(), knex('users').insert(). Raw pg: pool.query('SELECT * FROM users') — extract table name from SQL string literal. For each, build DbInteraction with table, operation (map findAll→read, create→create, update→update, destroy/delete→delete).

subtasks.title: Implement outbound call and auth detection
subtasks.description: Method extractOutboundCalls(servicePath): Find fetch() calls, axios.get/post/put/delete() calls, http.request() calls. Extract URL (first arg or config.url), method. Build OutboundCall. Method extractAuthScheme(servicePath): Look for: jwt/jsonwebtoken import → JWT scheme. passport import → OAuth/session scheme. Check middleware chain for auth-related names (authenticate, requireAuth, verifyToken). Check for Authorization header extraction in code. Return AuthScheme or null.

subtasks.title: Write integration tests for ExpressAnalyzer
subtasks.description: Create a sample Express app in tests/fixtures/express-app/ with: 3 routes (GET /users, POST /users, DELETE /users/:id), Prisma DB calls, one fetch() outbound call, JWT auth middleware. Run ExpressAnalyzer against it. Verify: 3 endpoints extracted with correct method/path, DB interactions found, outbound call found, auth scheme detected as JWT.

tasks.title: Implement FastAPIAnalyzer with tree-sitter Python Parsing
tasks.description: Build FastAPI analyzer using tree-sitter-python for Python AST parsing.
tasks.details: Parse Python decorators @app.get(), Pydantic models, SQLAlchemy patterns.
tasks.testStrategy: Parse sample FastAPI app. Routes, Pydantic schemas, SQLAlchemy calls extracted.

subtasks.title: Implement detect() for FastAPI
subtasks.description: Check for 'fastapi' in requirements.txt, Pipfile, or pyproject.toml [tool.poetry.dependencies] or [project.dependencies]. Also check for 'from fastapi import' in .py files as secondary signal.

subtasks.title: Set up tree-sitter-python parser
subtasks.description: Initialize tree-sitter with Python grammar. Function parsePythonFile(filePath): read file content, create tree via parser.parse(content). Return the syntax tree. Handle encoding (UTF-8). Handle parse errors gracefully.

subtasks.title: Extract FastAPI route decorators and function signatures
subtasks.description: Walk the tree-sitter AST. Find 'decorated_definition' nodes. Check if decorator matches @app.get/@app.post/@router.get etc. Extract route path from decorator arguments. Find the function definition below: extract parameter names and type annotations. Map type annotations to SchemaField types (str→string, int→number, bool→boolean). Detect Body(), Query(), Path() dependency injection parameters. Find Pydantic BaseModel subclasses for complex body schemas.

subtasks.title: Extract DB calls, outbound HTTP, and auth patterns
subtasks.description: DB: Find SQLAlchemy patterns (session.query, session.add, session.commit), Tortoise ORM (Model.create, Model.filter), raw SQL. Outbound: Find httpx.get/post, requests.get/post, aiohttp calls. Auth: Find Depends(get_current_user), OAuth2PasswordBearer, APIKeyHeader imports and usage.

subtasks.title: Write integration tests for FastAPIAnalyzer
subtasks.description: Create sample FastAPI app fixture with routes, Pydantic models, SQLAlchemy calls. Verify all extracted correctly.

tasks.title: Implement FlaskAnalyzer & GenericAnalyzer
tasks.description: Flask analyzer for @app.route patterns, and generic regex fallback.
tasks.details: Flask uses @app.route with methods=[]. Generic uses regex for any framework.
tasks.testStrategy: Flask routes extracted. Generic finds routes via regex in unknown frameworks.

subtasks.title: Implement FlaskAnalyzer
subtasks.description: Reuse tree-sitter-python parser from FastAPIAnalyzer. detect(): check for 'flask' in requirements.txt. extractEndpoints(): find @app.route('/path', methods=['GET']) and @blueprint.route() decorators. Extract path and methods from decorator kwargs. Find request.json, request.args, request.form access in function bodies. Find return jsonify() or make_response() for response shape.

subtasks.title: Implement GenericAnalyzer (regex fallback)
subtasks.description: detect(): Always returns true (registered with priority 0). Uses regex patterns to find routes in any language: Pattern for URL paths near HTTP methods: /\b(GET|POST|PUT|DELETE|PATCH)\s+['"](\/[\w\/:{}]+)['"]/. Pattern for common framework decorators: /@(Get|Post|Put|Delete)Mapping/, /\[Http(Get|Post|Put|Delete)\]/. Extract with lower confidence — set a 'confidence: low' flag on results. Useful for Spring Boot (if full Java analyzer not built) and .NET.

subtasks.title: Register all analyzers in default registry
subtasks.description: In default-registry.ts: import and register ExpressAnalyzer(100), FastAPIAnalyzer(90), FlaskAnalyzer(80), GenericAnalyzer(0). Verify resolve() picks the right one for each framework.

tasks.title: Implement AST Visitors: RouteVisitor, DbCallVisitor, OutboundHttpVisitor
tasks.description: Build the Visitor pattern from LLD Section 2.2 with CompositeVisitor.
tasks.details: Each visitor extracts one concern. CompositeVisitor runs all in single AST pass.
tasks.testStrategy: Each visitor works with AST fixtures. Composite returns combined results.

subtasks.title: Define ASTVisitor interface and VisitorContext
subtasks.description: In src/analyzer/visitors/interface.ts: Export interface ASTVisitor<T> { name: string; visit(node: Node, context: VisitorContext): T[]; }. Export interface VisitorContext { sourceFile: SourceFile; serviceName: string; filePath: string; }. The Node type comes from ts-morph.

subtasks.title: Implement RouteDefinitionVisitor
subtasks.description: Class RouteDefinitionVisitor implements ASTVisitor<EndpointDefinition>. visit(node, context): If node is CallExpression and matches route patterns (app.get, router.post, etc.), extract endpoint. Reuse logic from ExpressAnalyzer 8.2/8.3 but in visitor form. Return EndpointDefinition[] for this node (usually 0 or 1).

subtasks.title: Implement DbCallVisitor and OutboundHttpVisitor
subtasks.description: DbCallVisitor: visit() checks if node is CallExpression matching DB patterns (prisma.*, Model.find*, knex(), pool.query). Returns DbInteraction[]. OutboundHttpVisitor: visit() checks for fetch(), axios.*, http.request(). Returns OutboundCall[].

subtasks.title: Implement CompositeVisitor for single-pass traversal
subtasks.description: Class CompositeVisitor { private visitors: ASTVisitor<any>[]. register(visitor). async analyze(sourceFile, context): use sourceFile.forEachDescendant((node, traversal) => { for each visitor, call visit(node, context) and collect results }). Return { endpoints, dbInteractions, outboundCalls } aggregated from all visitors. This avoids multiple AST traversals per file. }

tasks.title: Implement working.md Document Generator
tasks.description: Build the markdown generator that produces working.md from ProjectAnalysis.
tasks.details: Structured markdown with service table, endpoint docs, dependency graph.

Set up console error capture: page.on('console', msg => if type==='error', collect). Initialize CrawlState with frontendUrl at depth 0. }

subtasks.title: Implement main BFS crawl loop
subtasks.description: While !crawlState.shouldStop(): dequeue target. Skip if visited. Mark visited. Create NetworkMonitor, attach to page. Navigate: page.goto(target.url, { waitUntil: 'networkidle', timeout }). Catch navigation errors (timeout, network error) → screenshot, mark as error, continue. Take screenshot: page.screenshot({ path, fullPage: true }). Check for login page via AuthHandler — if detected and not yet authenticated, authenticate with config.testCredentials. Detect forms via FormDetector — test each. Discover links: page.$$eval('a[href]', els => els.map(e => ({ href: e.href, text: e.textContent }))). Also discover buttons with onclick, nav elements. For each link: if same origin and not excluded, enqueue with depth+1 and referrer=current URL. Validate network requests against contracts. Build PageTestResult. Detach monitor.

subtasks.title: Implement SPA route detection
subtasks.description: For SPAs (React Router, Vue Router, etc.), clicking a link may not trigger a full navigation. After clicking a link: record page.url() before click. Use page.click(selector). Wait with Promise.race([page.waitForNavigation({timeout: 5000}).catch(() => null), page.waitForTimeout(3000)]). Check page.url() after — if changed, treat as new page. If URL didn't change but content did (check DOM changes), still treat as navigation. Handle hash-based routing (#/path) by including hash in normalization for SPA mode.
